summary: Investigated how to move gizmo from dev server to an installed application that runs at startup. Inspected the Tauri-based desktop app layout, confirmed the bun/rust/cargo/pnpm toolchain, and kicked off `pnpm desktop:build` to produce an installer. The Rust app compiled cleanly in 2m16s but MSI bundling failed because no `.ico` icon exists. Decided on a per-user Startup-folder shortcut to the installed Gizmo.exe over `tauri-plugin-autostart` (avoids a code change and second Rust build).
decisions: Install gizmo via its Tauri desktop installer rather than running it as a dev server.

Use a per-user Startup-folder shortcut to the installed Gizmo.exe for autostart instead of adding `tauri-plugin-autostart`, because the shortcut needs no code change or second Rust build and is easy to undo without admin rights.
errors: `pnpm desktop:build` (run in background as bky2ncq2m) compiled gizmo.exe successfully in 2m16s but failed at MSI bundling with `failed to bundle project: Couldn't find a .ico icon`; the Rust toolchain produced the binary, only the Wix-packaged MSI step failed.
A `sleep 120 && tail` polling attempt was blocked by the tool environment.
